summary: Donald R. Davis Jr. is an Indologist who studied under Richard W. Lariviere, Ludo Rocher, and Patrick Olivelle. He served as Associate Professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2012) and later joined the University of Texas at Austin faculty (attested 2026).

Donald S. Lopez Jr. is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his BA and PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. His career includes posts at Middlebury College (1986) and the University of Michigan (1990).

id: P:Dong Kam Tulku Ngawang Damchö Gyatso
summary: Dong Kam Tulku Ngawang Damchö Gyatso studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Dongak Chokyi Nyima studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Dongak Tendzin was a student and teacher of both Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Dongchu (1908–1977) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Minnan Buddhist Institute under Taixu, Aiting, and Nanting. He served as dean of Jiaoshan Buddhist Academy and abbot of Dinghui Monastery (1945–1949), and founded the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Culture.

Donna C. Kurtz is an archaeologist and historian. She studied at the University of Cincinnati, Yale University, and Somerville College before holding a post at the Classical Art Research Centre from circa 1970 to 2011.

Dor Bahadur Bista is a scholar in history and archaeology who studied at Tri-Chandra Multiple Campus. He served as a Professor at Tribhuvan University (attested 1988) and sat on the board of governors of the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development.
Doranne Jacobson works in Indology and anthropology. She completed her doctorate in anthropology at Columbia University, where she also served as a seminar associate at the Southern Asian Institute.

Doris Meth Srinivasan is a scholar of Indology and art history. She earned her BA from Hunter College and her PhD from the University of Pennsylvania, later working as Curator at the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art and Research Scholar at Stony Brook University.
Doris Unterthurner is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her MA at the University of Vienna under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

Dorje Rinchen (1819–1867) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He taught Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and studied under Sakya Yab Jé Kün Ga Rinchen, Chime Tenpai Nyima, and Sakya Dak Chen Ngawang Kün Ga Gyaltsen, among others.

Dorje Tseten (1925–2013) was a scholar in Tibetology and history. After completing an education degree at Beijing Normal University (1944–1948), he served as director of the China Tibetology Research Center from 1986 to 2000.

Dorji Banzarov (1822–1855) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and religion. He studied at the First Kazan Male Gymnasium and Kazan Imperial University under Józef Szczepan Kowalewski, completing his doctoral dissertation there in 1846.

Dorothy C. Wong specializes in Buddhist studies and art history. She has served as a visiting Professor of Buddhist Art at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2009) and as affiliate faculty at the University of Virginia (attested 2026).

Dosho Port is a figure in Buddhist studies who received traditional training under teachers including Dainin Katagiri, Toni Packer, Thich Nhat Hanh, Tangen Harada, Shodo Harada, John Daido Loori, and James Ishmael Ford.

Douglas Allen is a philosopher who studied at Yale, Banaras Hindu, and Vanderbilt Universities. He held faculty posts at Southern Illinois University, Central Connecticut State University, and the University of Maine, where he became Professor Emeritus in 2020.

Douglas Duckworth is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned degrees at James Madison University and the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, and later held posts at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute and East Tennessee State University.

Douglas Fairchild Ober is a scholar of history, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Washington and earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia under Harjot Oberoi.
Douglas Gildow is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He completed his PhD at Princeton University under the supervision of Stephen F. Teiser and Qi Zhou.
